character.name: Lord Galahad Orsival
character.age: Chronological: approximately three years and three months in local time plus roughly two weeks (rounded estimate). About one month old at planetfall, despite appearing five to six years old; subsequent age counts elapsed local time. Physically adult; bodily mature at about 3 metres (9 ft 10 in). Exact birthday unknown.
character.reputation: Royal Advisor, appointed this evening with a standing delegated Crown mandate for industry, infrastructure and defensive preparedness. Successful royal technical commissioner with the Marshal’s support and strengthened confidence among Desmaret’s company. Former Collegium scholar and present patron; not sovereign or operational commander.
character.weapons: None equipped. Vouressan-bone greatsword at the Orsival estate. Five House rifles approved and packed at the military works, awaiting delivery.
character.clothing: Charcoal coat, shirt, dark trousers and leather boots; travel-worn. Short white beard.
character.inventory: Personal effects and secured working notebooks; retained training report, ammunition returns, base-survey notes and authorised corridor intelligence extracts. Main cipher archive, recovered collections, greatsword and former Collegium belongings remain at the estate. No Hunter device acquired.
character.currency:
659 personal lorrats. Separate household funds: 1,160, of which 148 reserved and 1,012 uncommitted. Dorlac’s former 60 receivable was relinquished for goodwill; none remains due.

Commission pay: 150/month, paid on the first for the preceding month. On 01/11 received 70 commission pay and 40 final Collegium wages; salaried Collegium employment ended 20/10. Next commission payday 01/12. The 900 licence fee was already paid on 18/10.

State programme: 18,000 ceiling = 14,304 recognised cost + 180 outstanding commitments + 3,516 headroom. Not personal funds or profit. Expedition account closed, zero held; its complete settlement is preserved in the expedition accounts.

Commission accrual for 01–12/11: 60 unpaid, not cash. No new Advisor pay rate. Recorded programme headroom excludes an unpriced incremental return-transport valuation.
character.location: Auvrienne — audience with the Margrave and Marshal
character.condition: Bodily mature, uninjured and functional after completing training and returning by rail. Stable body–soul integration with no chronic pain; no new injury, fatigue penalty or mastered psychic technique.
character.language: Fluent local speech and independent reading and writing.
character.notes:
The railway watch initially accepted a Hunter-attack cover for Galahad’s killings; no actual Hunter appeared and no legal immunity was established.

Drossane’s six disguised attackers survived and reaffirmed service at Valdrec. A limited intelligence item was corroborated and correspondence arranged. The Margrave and senior commanders now know Galahad’s account; wider subversion remains his claim, not verified national control. No declared war follows. The 05–11/11 instruction assignment is complete; frontier commanders retain operational command. The Royal Advisor mandate does not grant command of an army in the field.

journal.title: Planetfall
journal.body: The incubation pod came to rest in a shattered planting bed beneath a ruined glasshouse roof. Its chamber, life support and integrated power remained functional. The fluid drained and the lid opened. Beyond the terrace lay jungle, a hillside railway and distant buildings beside dark water. Three adults approached aboard a small rail vehicle.

journal.title: First steps
journal.body: The subject climbed out, caught himself during an initial stumble and established his balance without injury. Close inspection revealed abundant sensory detail, though unfamiliar sounds and movement remained difficult to interpret. The rail vehicle stopped below and a voice called uphill.

journal.title: The voice below
journal.body: Recognising a bodily resemblance to the occupants, the subject approached and tried to imitate their call. A loose stair broke beneath him; the surviving railing prevented a fall. The first vocal imitation was distorted. A man with a lamp signalled him to stop while a companion raised a rifle. The lampholder touched his own chest and repeated “Veskan”.

journal.title: A name repeated
journal.body: The subject identified the wooden and metal object as a probable weapon. Two slow angled steps placed Veskan across its line; the bearer lowered the muzzle. With an open palm raised, the subject touched his own chest and reproduced “Veskan” clearly. Veskan repeated his stopping gesture, then demonstrated the distinction between himself and the child. The vehicle’s engine was switched off.

journal.title: An offer of warmth
journal.body: The subject stopped, pointed to Veskan and repeated his name, then pointed to himself, hesitated and nodded. Veskan acknowledged the exchange without naming him. After speaking with his companions, he received a heavy grey cloth, placed the lamp on a trackside bracket and demonstrated wrapping the cloth around his shoulders. He held it open toward the child while the armed man kept his weapon low and watched the vegetation.

journal.title: Cloth and speech
journal.body: The subject accepted the heavy grey cloth and wrapped it around himself as demonstrated. He continued copying the patrol’s speech. Isolated sounds could be reproduced, but connected speech remained difficult to divide and interpret. Veskan repeated gestures alongside sounds. The rifleman lowered his weapon away from the subject, and Veskan demonstrated the trolley footboard.

journal.title: Departure by rail
journal.body: The subject boarded voluntarily, studying the vehicle while remaining cautious about the occupants’ intentions. He observed the brake linkage and the engine’s connection to the moving drive. Veskan left the entrance chain unfastened and gestured to warn of the hot cover. The driver restarted the engine and released the brakes. The trolley began descending toward distant lights, leaving the pod in the ruined glasshouse.

journal.title: Serravonne
journal.body: During the journey the subject watched the machinery and practised speech. Repeated gestures gave familiar sounds concrete meanings, while longer exchanges remained difficult. The trolley reached Serravonne, a fortified coastal settlement with a cleared perimeter, guarded rail gate and industrial yards. Following a brief exchange with the gate guards, the patrol entered and stopped beside a lit station building.

journal.title: A room of purposes
journal.body: The subject followed Veskan indoors. Clothing, boots, walls, windows and doors revealed practical functions through observation. The woman with the ledger demonstrated how opening the stove vent strengthened the fire and used cloth to handle the hot kettle. Words for objects and simple actions were repeated and distinguished. Water from a separate covered jug was offered in a chipped enamel cup.

journal.title: The first drink
journal.body: The subject lifted the cup and sniffed the water. Detecting no obvious foul or irritating odour, he drank it all and repeated “Drink”. The woman then demonstrated “Cup”. The subject correctly repeated that word while raising the vessel, identified Veskan and indicated himself without supplying a name. The empty cup remained in his hand.

journal.title: A place for the night
journal.body: The woman introduced herself as Corva. Lessons continued alongside a discussion the subject could only partly follow. Corva used a wall telephone and wrote in her ledger. Workers brought bedding and a folding canvas bed, which she prepared in a cleared alcove beside the kitchen. A gate man spoke with her, observed the preparations and left. Corva placed a bowl of warm grain-and-vegetable food and a spoon beside the bed. Veskan returned to the yard. Corva then invited the subject toward the alcove.

journal.title: A week at the station
journal.body: The subject stayed with Corva, learning through conversation, repetition and exploration. Meals and bedding became routine; she supplied a shirt, drawstring trousers and soft leather shoes. The grey cloth remained with the bedding. Familiar speech became usable, though unfamiliar context and abstract vocabulary still required explanation. Corva began addressing him as “little scholar”, without assigning a personal name. No attack occurred during the week.

journal.title: Machinery and a visitor
journal.body: Exploration included the storeroom, washroom, workshop, drainage channels and warning bells. Hinges, catches, pulleys, taps and a demonstrated valve revealed useful relationships. The yard pump’s intermittent pressure fault remained unresolved. Its mechanic removed the cover and allowed observation. Corva then brought the subject to Veskan, whose report announced the railway superintendent’s interest. Corva arranged the meeting here for the following morning. The patrol report still needed a name; none was supplied.

journal.title: Answers and the hunters
journal.body: The subject answered confidently, described his missing knowledge of his origin, and explained his deductions about the alarms and people’s unease at his arrival from the sky. Corva supplied the word “answers”. Veskan distinguished animal, fire and railway warnings from hunter alarms. Both adults explained that the hunters descend in flying machines and hunt humans and animals. The purpose of a particular visit is not always known.

journal.title: Words without moving mouths
journal.body: The subject disclosed hearing things people did not speak aloud. Corva asked for examples rather than treating the report as wrongdoing. An impression of the telephone and “Who could I ask?” accompanied her apparent voice while her lips remained still. Earlier in the week, a fleeting impression of black water and a slipping hand had occurred near the pump; its source remained unidentified.

journal.title: Memories reaching across
journal.body: The subject described an early sense of safety with Veskan, glimpses of another boy in his care, and fragments accompanying Corva’s lessons. Veskan disclosed that he had a son, killed when the hunters struck the line. A brief impression of a small grease-marked hand within a larger hand followed. Corva described remembering her mother’s stove with a broken catch while teaching about the station stove. Associated movement and meaning were clearer to the subject than any complete remembered scene. Both adults agreed to be careful whom they told.

journal.title: A place remains
journal.body: The subject said the reception happened all the time, could not be stopped and was helpful; he did not wish to stop learning through it. He told Veskan that the boy had been happy and linked this to feeling safe. Veskan was grateful. Corva explained that receiving something useful could still be difficult for the person whose memory it was. They offered help distinguishing speech, impressions and interpretation. Veskan affirmed that the subject could stay. Both adults intended to attend tomorrow’s meeting. Veskan left for the yard; Corva put the report beneath her ledger and offered a pause. The pump remained dismantled, and the next activity was left open.

journal.title: The superintendent arrives
journal.body: After following his usual routine and sleeping, the subject met railway superintendent Leont Vardesca in the station maintenance room on a rainy morning. Corva and Veskan attended. Vardesca asked for the earliest remembered events and explained his concern for people working near the landing site.

journal.title: An account of planetfall
journal.body: The subject recalled rumbling, crashing, a sudden stop and the draining fluid, followed by leaving the chamber and seeing Veskan. He clarified that the chamber opened by itself after it stopped moving. Veskan confirmed wet ground around the apparatus and reported that it had not been moved. Vardesca instructed the patrol to prevent entry or dismantling pending further assessment.

journal.title: Care authorised
journal.body: Asked whether he wanted to remain with Corva, the subject nodded. Vardesca authorised meals and necessary clothing on the station account, with supervision in the working yard. He retained responsibility for the report and asked to be notified before anyone seeking the child was brought to him. Written confirmation of the care arrangement was promised.

journal.title: Galahad
journal.body: A brief inward whisper preceded the choice: “Galahad. I want to be called Galahad.” The voice seemed both his own and unfamiliar; no source was identified. Asked whether the name was remembered or newly thought of, he answered that it was his name and the one he chose. Corva entered Galahad in her ledger, and Vardesca recorded it in his notebook and demonstrated its written form. Veskan recognised the choice. No surname was introduced.

journal.title: Ideas made real
journal.body: Galahad described machines as “a web of ideas made real”, explaining that he wanted to understand their purposes, functions and design choices. Vardesca discussed cost, casting, available power, repair access and copied designs, referring to an expensive old harbour pump. Galahad said he did not yet understand enough to propose improvements. No invention, diagnosis or repair was claimed.

journal.title: The meeting concludes
journal.body: Vardesca offered to speak to the workshop foreman about safe, supervised explanations when staff had time. He also intended to arrange an inspection of the pod, which was to remain undisturbed. The superintendent departed with Veskan; Corva checked Galahad’s new ledger entry and carried the kettle toward the kitchen. The interview ended with continued shelter confirmed and learning opportunities promised.

journal.title: Books and concealed understanding
journal.body: Galahad became fluent in speech, reading and writing, rapidly absorbing the accessible books. Arithmetic led to algebra, geometry and surveying calculations; manuals supplied mechanics, heat and electricity. Maps, shipping tables, newspapers and histories expanded his knowledge of the world and exposed conflicting accounts. Corva and Veskan found further books, but advanced references remained difficult to obtain. Galahad concealed much of his understanding; rapid growth and glimpses of his work nevertheless led some workers to suspect more.

journal.title: Work among the engines
journal.body: Vardesca’s promise led to supervised workshop access, then useful maintenance and small repairs. A small utility knife was issued for ordinary tasks. Galahad learned familiar engines and fault relationships, while equipment access and available materials constrained fabrication. A discarded small engine was restored to motion but remained uneven under load. His clothing was replaced and his alcove bed lengthened as he grew toward Corva’s height.

journal.title: A damaged line
journal.body: Hunters struck a pumping installation farther along the railway. Galahad encountered the aftermath rather than the attack: injured workers returned, deliveries were disrupted and repairs displaced lessons for several weeks.

journal.title: Private control
journal.body: Solitary practice progressed from moving a washer to lifting and rotating small objects with precision, and briefly suspending a heavy engine assembly. Fine control was harder than gross lifting. Distraction reduced precision; sustained effort brought hunger and fatigue. In quiet surroundings Galahad could sometimes reduce received mental impressions, though crowds and strong emotions remained intrusive. No lasting psychic mechanism or new material resulted.

journal.title: Beyond the perimeter
journal.body: Repeated secret night excursions established short routes and familiar landmarks beyond the walls. No one confronted Galahad about the outings. A rain-swollen crossing collapsed beneath him and drove him against submerged stone, opening his flank. He escaped through his own strength; the wound healed quickly but hurt during movement for several nights. No hunter was encountered face to face and no alien equipment was recovered.

journal.title: An unfinished challenge
journal.body: Galahad privately attempted to construct a firearm from available parts without dismantling an existing example. Several attempts were discarded. The remaining prototype was incomplete and unreliable, with no dependable ammunition supply. It stayed concealed with his work rather than accompanying his night journeys.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and eight days • Evening
journal.title: The academy reply
journal.body: Corva presented the academy’s reply to her request for books. It required examples of mathematics, mechanical reasoning and completed work. Galahad deferred to her experience. She proposed truthful examples and a covering letter that omitted his arrival, while leaving the selection of work to him. Any meeting remained a possibility to consider later; no admission, book loan or assessment had been granted.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and eight days • Evening
journal.title: Mum
journal.body: Galahad casually thanked Corva as Mum, recognising her parental role. She was visibly moved, touched his forearm and accepted the address. A warm impression of the old kitchen alcove accompanied the moment. Galahad began preparing restrained examples using existing books and notebooks. Corva drafted the covering letter and replaced a word near its beginning with “My son”.

journal.date: Thirteen days before the Collegium reply
journal.title: The selected packet
journal.body: Galahad handed his deliberately restrained designs to Corva. She enclosed them with her covering letter and sent the packet north to the Auvrienne Collegium of Civil Engineering. Study and tinkering continued through the following thirteen days. The small engine remained irregular under sustained load.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: Verification requested
journal.body: The Collegium returned the drawings with two letters and a printed assessment sheet. Examiner Odran Savel acknowledged correct results but questioned missing derivations and inconsistent levels of exposition. The advanced-book loan was withheld pending independent verification. A supervised exercise in Auvrienne was offered; Corva suggested asking whether local railway testimony could establish the work first.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: The housing and its promise
journal.body: Galahad suspected jealousy or class prejudice behind the response. Corva acknowledged the possibility without claiming to know Savel’s motives. Galahad explained the housing’s struts and linkage points, projecting several decades of additional service for less than a kilogram of extra material. Corva understood the rationale and asked what supported the lifespan estimate.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: Three piles
journal.body: Galahad retrieved a large body of papers from beneath his bed and divided it into first proofs, second iterations and basic testing, and current work. Corva recognised the extent of his research and apologised for assuming he had not already done the work. She proposed showing enough to answer the examiner while retaining the originals.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: Beyond the engine
journal.body: The aligned pages also contained energy, lubrication and aerodynamic workings, military and economic projections for a unified eastern Vesalius, political philosophy and divination research. Galahad reported successful improvements over common divination practices in his own tests. Corva promised to keep the mixed papers at home for now and proposed copying relevant engineering work onto clean sheets.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: Power and opposition
journal.body: Galahad specified unification under one government, doubted voluntary cooperation between the existing states and preferred infamy to ignominy. He argued that victory determines whose history endures and treated morality as subordinate to survival. Corva questioned what would happen to dissenters and how fear might distort official reports. She affirmed that she would ask difficult questions because he was her son.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and twenty-one days • Afternoon
journal.title: Into the stars
journal.body: Galahad challenged the usefulness of dishonest reports and described the desired result of his government: safety, stability and an everlasting future for his people, reaching into the stars and beyond. Corva clarified that a lie could serve a frightened official while harming government. She supported the hope of a better future, wanted to remain free to question his methods, and drew the copying paper closer. “Tell me where you think it begins.”

journal.date: Following the first reply • Twenty-three days
journal.title: The copied proofs
journal.body: Corva and Galahad copied relevant engineering proofs and added selective advanced passages to interest the Collegium. Originals, political projections and divination workings remained at home. The packet was sent.

journal.title: An even beat
journal.body: The small engine ran steadily through the available workshop load test. A mechanic noticed the improvement and stayed to observe the remainder.

journal.title: The Vouressan
journal.body: Galahad recognised a house-sized Vouressan from his reading and killed it barehanded in the wilds. Its flame burned his outer forearm and damaged a sleeve. The wound healed over the following days. No human witnessed the kill.

journal.title: White bone
journal.body: Galahad fashioned a guardless greatsword and integral grip from one piece of the Vouressan’s exceptionally strong white cranial bone. He inscribed protective forms from his reading, practised its use on night hunts and kept it wrapped beneath his bed behind the papers.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-four days • Afternoon
journal.title: A different reply
journal.body: Savel accepted the supplied housing derivation and withdrew his concern about preparation for that portion. He questioned the conditions governing an advanced result and recognised deliberate omissions. He proposed fuller discussion with a workshop instructor attending. No advanced books or unrestricted loan accompanied the reply.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-four days • Afternoon
journal.title: Hunting
journal.body: When Corva asked about his night departures, Galahad unwrapped the sword on the kitchen table. He described killing its source without a weapon and making a useful, valuable blade to provide for her and Veskan if necessary. Corva was moved, affirmed his place at home and warned that prospective buyers might take an interest in him as well as the sword.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-four days • Afternoon and evening
journal.title: Tomorrow
journal.body: Galahad identified the creature as a Vouressan, said the injury had healed and chose to travel alone by train the next day. Corva telephoned for arrangements. No passenger seat was available; she asked the goods-train guard to help. A message to the Collegium could be passed through the railway office, but no reply arrived.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Before dawn
journal.title: Leaving home
journal.body: Galahad bound the wrapped sword with household rope and left his other belongings at home. Veskan returned his farewell embrace and urged him to find proper lodging. Galahad kissed Corva’s forehead; she reminded him where he could return. The guard admitted him to the brake van and accepted his explanation that the bundle was artwork for appraisal.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Evening
journal.title: Auvrienne
journal.body: A sixteen-hour goods-train journey carried Galahad through defended coastal valleys, with a lengthy junction delay. Auvrienne’s freight yards, furnace-lit workshops, terraces and fortified railway cutting gave way to a busy unloading canopy. He arrived alert and physically capable, carrying the covered sword.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Evening
journal.title: Through the gate
journal.body: Galahad told the railway watchman that the bundle was artwork being appraised. The watchman advised keeping it wrapped on the tram and let him pass. Outside lay a sloping avenue, booking office, public street plan, trams, an uphill monument and inn, and a bookseller closing for the evening. No next destination has been chosen.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Late evening
journal.title: Reading the city
journal.body: Several hours of walking connected the street plan with central Auvrienne’s rail basin, terraced roads, stairs, drainage and tramways. Galahad reached the Collegium after teaching hours; the porter said Savel had gone home.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Late evening
journal.title: An address freely offered
journal.body: Subconscious psychic pressure eased the porter into trust. He gave Savel’s address: 37 Rue Cendravel, upstairs over the bookbinder, with a side door and brass bell. He cautioned that an address did not guarantee a welcome and still asked for a name.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Late evening
journal.title: The late knock
journal.body: Galahad’s powerful knock boomed through the stairwell without damaging the door. A curtain moved across the street. Savel answered, initially alarmed and then irritated by the late hour.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Late evening
journal.title: Savel opens the door
journal.body: Galahad named himself and declared that Savel would organise lodging and Collegium attendance. A renewed influence of trust softened the response. Savel recognised Corva’s son, offered his spare room for the night and help at the office the following morning.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and forty-five days • Late evening
journal.title: Proofs beneath the lamp
journal.body: Galahad spent the night explaining selected mathematics and engineering. Savel followed the missing steps, became absorbed and asked more precise questions. He also saw the sword, accepting the account of raw bone bought from a trader; he advised keeping the valuable blade covered and in Galahad’s room.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and fifty-two days • Evening
journal.title: A place at the Collegium
journal.body: During the week Savel secured provisional enrolment and a small bursary covering a room and meals. Ordinary library access and loans became available. Galahad moved into a lockable room in the residential annex; the sword went beneath the bed.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and fifty-two days • Evening
journal.title: Calling home
journal.body: Galahad telephoned Corva with his enrolment and lodging arrangements, explained his intention to stay and study, and asked her to contact him immediately if needed. She could reach him through the Collegium office and asked him to keep calling.

journal.date: Planetfall + one local year and fifty-two days • Evening
journal.title: A bird among the papers
journal.body: Library study rapidly expanded available mathematical, mechanical and scientific references. In private, Galahad fashioned an intricate wind-up bird from scrap. It hopped and chirped until its stored energy ran out. Savel offered a next-morning workshop exercise involving a faulty governor; no response to that offer was recorded.

journal.title: An independent course
journal.body: After the second month, each subject received a weekly individual hour instead of ordinary classes. Full curricula and syllabuses supported self-directed work. By four months, Galahad had completed three years of curriculum and read approximately three quarters of the Collegium’s library.

journal.title: Structures on paper
journal.body: Monumental buildings and elevated galleries passed examination of their structural calculations. Their expense and the necessary industrial resources remained substantial. No construction commission followed.

journal.title: An altered atmosphere
journal.body: Repeated psychic practice made comfort, trust, unease and fear more targeted. Visitors often departed and requests received easier hearings. Some students became distant; nobody confronted Galahad with a psychic-interference accusation. Teachers still questioned his work.

journal.title: The mechanical snake
journal.body: More than a hundred thousand tiny functional and decorative pieces formed a piston-driven articulated snake. Contact pressure redirected it at obstacles. Recirculating water served as working fluid with a separate fuel charge, allowing an hour’s operation under suitable conditions. His enhanced vision and dexterity made magnification helpful rather than necessary.

journal.title: Green light in the wilds
journal.body: Weekly hunts around Auvrienne alternated sword use and psychic practice. Green lightning manifested lethally against prey and became easier to direct. Larger discharges left conspicuous sound and scorched surfaces. No hunter appeared. Calls to Corva and Veskan continued throughout the months.

journal.date: Four months after Collegium enrolment • Evening
journal.title: An introduction offered
journal.body: With the snake moving beneath Galahad’s desk, Savel knocked and offered to introduce a visiting works engineer the following afternoon. The engineer was willing to examine the larger structural designs. Galahad has not yet answered.

journal.date: Four months and one week after Collegium enrolment
journal.title: Clothing for a growing scholar
journal.body: Approaching eight feet, Galahad could no longer use borrowed clothing. Savel arranged tailored garments through the Collegium account: charcoal coat, pale shirts, dark trousers and larger boots.

journal.date: Four months and one week after Collegium enrolment
journal.title: Ottrel Cevrane
journal.body: The works engineer examined Galahad’s structural drawings and discussed practical installations. Calming influence eased the meeting; substantial technical understanding sustained it. Cevrane supplied operating returns and offered a pumping-works visit.

journal.date: Four months and one week after Collegium enrolment
journal.title: First protective charms
journal.body: Hunted bone, teeth, scale and hide became intricate traditional charms. Fine emerald sparks improved the charred borders after damaged early blanks. Persistent protection was not established.

journal.title: The southern pumping works
journal.body: Galahad visited with budgeted material and flow proposals. Adjusted to site conditions, changes were implemented in stages. Returns showed reduced vibration, steadier delivery and fewer interruptions; Cevrane shared the credit.

journal.title: Resident scholar
journal.body: All prescribed curricula were completed and every Collegium library book read twice. Galahad became a resident researcher and occasional teacher across subjects, gaining contacts among students, faculty and professional households.

journal.title: Work of Galahad
journal.body: Iseva Dorlac sold forty attributed charms and retained one quarter of retail receipts. Galahad described an exclusive supplier in Ceralte; the materials actually came from his private hunts.

journal.title: The older arts
journal.body: Valesse Orchant witnessed an emerald spark and taught attention, association and the relation between sign, material and purpose. Some pieces retained faint impressions for hours. Protection against misfortune remained unverified.

journal.date: Ten months and one week after Collegium enrolment
journal.title: Support for home
journal.body: Calls continued at least fortnightly. Corva and Veskan each received 180 lorrats. After recorded income and expenses, 630 lorrats remained, principally on deposit. Galahad reached eight and a half feet, still growing at a slowing pace.

journal.date: Ten months and one week after Collegium enrolment
journal.title: An invitation from the chancery
journal.body: Rumours of his interest in advising the Margrave accompanied reports of his accomplishments. Savel delivered an invitation to present practical work before a chancery official four days later.

journal.title: An exclusive supplier
journal.body: Galahad told Dorlac that his supposed old friend would deal only with him. She accepted exclusivity for now, hoping it would support prices, and declined to promise unavailable quantities.

journal.date: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment • Morning
journal.title: The upper precinct
journal.body: Galahad presented his invitation, returns and selected mathematical advancements while sustaining a broad calming presence. His absent surname drew class-conscious scrutiny despite the welcoming influence.

journal.date: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment • Morning
journal.title: The Orsival connection
journal.body: Galahad supplied Corva’s family name. Cyrrel Vaust noted “family connection stated; institutional sponsor confirmed.” Legal surname registration remained unresolved; Collegium sponsorship sufficed for the meeting.

journal.date: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment • Morning
journal.title: Money and influence
journal.body: Galahad intensified his calming pressure and offered 100 lorrats. Vaust accepted the money privately without receipt, then proposed a sixty-lorrat technical commission subject to expenditure approval. Savings fell to 530.

journal.date: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment • Afternoon
journal.title: A commission authorised
journal.body: Galahad accepted. Approval arrived before closing. The assignment covers the southern pumping works and uphill delivery main, with an attributed costed report requested within three weeks and access to relevant records and accompanied inspections.

journal.date: Ten months and eleven days after Collegium enrolment • Evening
journal.title: The delivery main
journal.body: Galahad returned to his room with plans, operating logs, repair accounts and authorisation. Different daily reporting cutoffs were identified; the broader discrepancy remains unresolved. The bursar credited the thirty-lorrat advance, bringing funds to 560; thirty more is due on delivery.

journal.date: Ten months and eighteen days after enrolment
journal.title: The whole network
journal.body: Accompanied access expanded to every section. Galahad submitted a full modular redesign preserving useful infrastructure and district supply. Differing daily cutoffs, wear and poor coordination explain the southern discrepancy, without demonstrated theft. Estimated installed cost for each module is below its corresponding annual repair allowance. Cevrane endorsed a witnessed first installation.

journal.title: Patronage sought
journal.body: Galahad returned the 30-lorrat advance and paid Vaust a further 150. He requested minor hereditary House Orsival, land near Serravonne and a sponsored worldwide Collegium expedition in place of the fee. Vaust supported the requests; funds fell to 380.

journal.title: Service and confidence
journal.body: Galahad offered technical, military and diplomatic intelligence, and service conditional on the requested patronage. Vaust accepted the assurance, apologised for his phrasing about confidentiality, and prepared a favourable recommendation. He recorded interest in an advisory office without promising it.

journal.title: Both parents
journal.body: Galahad supplied Veskan Orsival’s name. Vaust included both parents beneath Galahad as proposed house head, signed his recommendation and sent it for preliminary consideration.

journal.title: Successors and continuity
journal.body: The Collegium endorsed the expedition. Professors nominated their successors; Savel remained to preserve teaching and receive duplicate reports. Five nominees accepted. The first pumping module entered service successfully, supporting the petition.

journal.title: Private observations
journal.body: Galahad maintained research, teaching, hunts, crafting and family calls. A new private notebook recorded magic experiments; small emerald discharges became more repeatable, while protection from misfortune remained unproven. Three charms sold; other pieces remained on consignment. Net income less expenses brought personal funds to 473 lorrats.

journal.title: House Orsival
journal.body: The Margrave’s grant recognised Lord Galahad Orsival as founder and head of a minor hereditary house, Lady Corva as Mother of the House and Sir Veskan as Father of the House. A 56-hectare estate near Serravonne was granted with existing tenancies protected.

journal.title: A year abroad
journal.body: A one-year expedition was approved with Galahad as scholarly director and 10,000 lorrats in Chancery sponsorship, joined by 4,500 from the Collegium in a separate operating fund. The Collegium continues ordinary wages and institutional support. Varcet, Rouvant, Sarnot, Tessier and Aubrel accepted places. Departure through Ceralte was fixed for twenty-one days hence. The former examination fee was superseded by patronage; no personal advisory appointment was granted.

journal.title: Railway-yard standoff
journal.body: Galahad travelled home by train, taking coffee and a snack. At the yard he found Corva holding Veskan, shot in the upper arm and beaten across the face after offering a week’s wages and asking for time for an indebted subordinate. Orvasse and armed Scerault men confront frightened railway workers. Galahad pushed to the front and demanded an explanation. His sword remains at the Collegium; no retaliation, further shot, treatment or resolution has occurred. The family has not yet heard about its elevation.

journal.title: The railway-yard killings
journal.body: Galahad killed Orvasse and all the Scerault men present after declaring his name and sentence. Psychic fear drove the gang to scatter; no actual Hunter appeared. He then replaced the pressure with calm, requested the authorities and prompted the witnesses to describe a Hunter attack. He knelt beside Corva and Veskan and attempted to help his father.

journal.title: A home for the Orsivals
journal.body: The responding watch initially accepted the witnesses’ account. Railway transport brought the family to the estate without a personal charge. Galahad carried Veskan inside and summoned a surgeon, who assessed the arm wound, concussion and facial injuries. Lucette Marcenay received a 25-lorrat gift for her prompt care and prepared a light meal.

journal.title: Recovery and household authority
journal.body: Veskan improved with rest, medical care and Galahad’s attention; small superficial cuts responded to repeated psychic healing. Corva received authority over house finances, staffing and maintenance. Both parents heard the one-year expedition plan and were told that the estate was their home. Galahad designated a study, library/archive room and future workshop, and reviewed the land and repair needs with Corva and Lucette.

journal.date: Three days at the estate · corrected accounts
journal.title: The first household budget
journal.body: The reconciled ledger records 402 lorrats held, of which 282 are earmarked and 120 uncommitted. The separate expedition appropriation is untouched. Lucette’s pay is 14 per month plus room and meals. The central estate forecast leaves 218 annually after working, shared and household allowances; rents, harvests, timber and payment dates still need verification. No projected revenue has been credited as cash.

journal.date: Evening before departure · twenty days after approval
journal.title: Ready for the first passage
journal.body: After further days with his parents, Galahad returned to Auvrienne and completed expedition preparations. Rail passage through Serravonne and sea passage to Dalmor are booked with space appropriate to his size. Ordinary entry, transit and declared-instrument permissions cover the itinerary; seasonal passages, paid lodging and onward transport are arranged. Restricted research access is handled separately. Departure is in northern autumn, placing northern sailings in their service seasons. The five scholars have parallel academic assignments and Savel will receive duplicate reports. Equipment and opening transport cost 510 from the expedition fund. Limited estate repairs cost 18 and his personal return journey cost 6, leaving personal cash of 378. No projected revenue has been credited as cash. The expedition has not departed.

journal.title: Across the first six capitals
journal.body: Surface travel and full visits to Dalmor, Varnessa, Gavrielle, Serevienne, Kelbrienne and Miravelle brought the party to Drossane. Fifty-one travel days and thirty-four full visiting days elapsed, with no contingency used. Multidisciplinary study, scholarly reports and four reciprocal correspondents expanded Galahad’s knowledge and access. Simple psychic impressions now reliably persist for several days. Settled accounts: personal 522; expedition 11,430. Family letters report Veskan healing well; the household statement is pending.

journal.title: The assay-office collection
journal.body: Sarvelle presented surviving waterworks papers, material trials and a damaged purported sighting assembly. Varcet, Rouvant, Sarnot and Tessier attended. External study led Galahad privately toward a plasma-emitter hypothesis. He publicly suggested an ocular device and departed politely; the object remains office property.

journal.title: Papers put away; breakfast briefing
journal.body: After a sleepless but unimpaired night of technical reconstruction, Galahad concealed his manuscript among other papers and began a private contextual cipher. He joined breakfast, reviewed the scholars’ assignments and arranged evening reports. The scene stops with all six still inside the guesthouse.

journal.title: The guesthouse confrontation
journal.body: Six apparent Karsenne officers raised firearms at the expedition. Galahad shielded his scholars, immobilised all six attackers and their weapons, and spread psychic terror through the nearby crowd. Forced searches of two men’s memories revealed a Caldrienne assassination operation intended to damage Veyrasse–Karsenne relations. No shot was fired.

journal.title: A provisional cell
journal.body: Galahad released the restraint under calming influence and accepted the men’s disarmament. He privately ordered a false account of their defeat and future service, promising rewards and threatening them and their loved ones for betrayal. A deliberate image and voice reached all six minds, showing his intended march into Valdrec. They accepted; no binding loyalty, communication system, completed report or invasion followed.

journal.title: Old friends, publicly
journal.body: Galahad dismissed the six with a friendly public greeting and called the encounter a foolish joke by old friends. The operatives recovered their firearms and departed downhill. All five scholars remain uninjured but shaken outside the guesthouse; they did not receive the private projection. Tessier asks whether to carry on. No further travel, fieldwork, payment or injury has occurred.

journal.title: Expedition return and maturity
journal.body: Returned to Auvrienne on day 355 with all five scholars uninjured and ten reserve days unused. Mature at about 3 m, with a short white beard. Forty recurring correspondents, an unnamed six-practitioner Order, two recovered psychic collections and thousands of ciphered private pages extend his work. No Hunter technology acquired.

journal.title: Accounts and institutional debriefings
journal.body: Official reports inventoried; Chancery transcription begun and civil-engineering briefings completed. Both sponsors approved 500 scholar awards, 645 leadership award and 1,500 refunds. Personal funds 1,197; separate estate 314; expedition fund closed. Veskan’s arm healed and workshop building repaired, still unequipped.

journal.title: Royal technical commission accepted
journal.body: Darscelet and Vaucerin supported a private audience with Odrienne. Galahad presented the unbuilt rifle and preliminary carrier and reported his Caldrienne cell. He accepted the signed technical commission. Royal Advisor review follows a produced rifle trial shipment and controlled demonstration. A week at Serravonne is planned; facility preparations, costed allocation and remuneration remain pending. No departure or new grant yet.

journal.title: Homecoming
journal.body: After six lorrats for the overnight train and about six hours of rest, Galahad walked home to Corva and Veskan. He placed 1,000 in household funds and authorised both parents to pursue informed investments, including outside the estate.

journal.title: Household preparations
journal.body: A private warning about possible Caldrienne risks prompted two trained watchhounds; armed guards remain prospective. A telephone was installed, tenant drain and roof defects addressed, and grievances recorded. Dorlac was allowed to retain 60 for goodwill and met the parents; no new enterprise was purchased.

journal.title: The return run and agreement
journal.body: Galahad reached Auvrienne by a concealed unaided cross-country run in a little over three hours, uninjured and without a known witness. He signed the commission agreement before the Marshal, then entered the allocated works. State ceiling 18,000; licence 900; commission pay 150/month.

journal.title: First development rifles
journal.body: After overnight workshop reorganisation, three development rifles were assembled. Core staff arrived under foreman Bastien Ordel and liaison Captain Armand Serault. Controlled firing subsequently passed. The 900 licence fee was paid.

journal.title: Collegium patronage
journal.body: Galahad resigned salaried employment, donated 500 from personal funds and offered unpaid consultation and occasional teaching. Personal belongings and private collections reached the estate on 22/10; institutional property was returned and his room released.

journal.title: First week return
journal.body: The works held three development rifles and 120 trial rifles: 96 accepted, eighteen awaiting tests and six for correction. Recognised programme cost was 9,395, outstanding commitments 950 and uncommitted headroom 7,655. These are historical cumulative figures.

journal.title: The enlarged trial batch
journal.body: The original 120 cleared acceptance on 27/10. Staff then completed another 72 under Ordel, demonstrating twelve per production day without Galahad doing assembly. A written one-off licence extension covered the enlarged batch within the state ceiling.

journal.title: Accounts settled
journal.body: Seventy commission pay and forty final Collegium wages were received. Household funds paid fourteen for Lucette and two for telephone rental. Collegium payroll is closed; commission pay continues monthly.

journal.title: Production paused; report submitted
journal.body: Final inventory: 192 accepted trial rifles, split 187 military and five approved for House Orsival, plus three retained development rifles. All remain at the works awaiting the relevant dispatch. Programme: 13,220 cost, 180 commitments and 4,600 headroom. Personal funds 659; household 1,160. The Marshal and Darscelet will meet Galahad on 03/11 at nine to settle transport and demonstration. No border journey or Advisor appointment has occurred.

journal.title: Training authority and dispatch settled
journal.body: The Marshal and Darscelet approve seven full training days, 05–11/11, for Captain Lucard Desmaret’s 160-person company. Galahad directs instruction and technical certification; Desmaret retains discipline and administration, and the frontier chain retains operational command. No attack order or Royal Advisor appointment.

journal.title: Arrival at Cressault
journal.body: Galahad and Serault accompany 187 rifles and 12,000 rounds by rail from Auvrienne to Cressault. Five House rifles still await delivery and three development rifles remain at the works. After final checks, ammunition issue, transport and payroll, recognised programme costs are 14,024, commitments 180 and headroom 3,796.

journal.title: Private trial and a larger purpose
journal.body: Desmaret fires twelve ordinary rounds without stoppage; Galahad’s ten rapid shots leave one entry point with almost no visible recoil. Discussion turns to unity and defence against the Hunters. Respect deepens without a political oath. Twenty-two rounds spent; 11,978 remain. Intelligence briefing requested.

journal.title: First training day complete
journal.body: Receipt confirmed: 160 rifles issued, 27 reserve. Instruction and soldier conversations build confidence. The day expends 1,620 ordinary rounds; 10,358 remain (8,000 armour-piercing, 2,358 ordinary). One of seven days complete. Major Vauzel confirms 06/11 at 18:00 with operations staff; Desmaret accompanies Galahad. Programme reconciled through 05/11: 14,059 recognised cost + 180 commitments + 3,761 headroom = 18,000. Personal 659 and household 1,160 unchanged.

journal.title: The base as a working system
journal.body: Galahad surveys billets, clothing and drying, food, water, maintenance, parts, fuel, stores, readiness and defensive works. He records bottlenecks and dependencies without ordering a new programme or treating one base as a district-wide inventory.

journal.title: Second training day complete
journal.body: NCOs increasingly correct mistakes independently and slower groups improve. Two of seven days complete; five remain. Training expends 800 ordinary rounds, leaving 9,558: 8,000 armour-piercing and 1,558 ordinary. Serault raises a top-up through stores, with quantity and valuation due before draw. Programme costs now 14,094, commitments 180 and headroom 3,726. Personal and household cash remain unchanged.

journal.title: The corridor appreciation
journal.body: At district headquarters Vauzel and an operations officer brief Galahad and Desmaret. Caldrienne has an estimated 18,400 corridor personnel (16,000–21,500), 110 serviceable armoured vehicles (96–124), 160 artillery pieces excluding mortars (144–180), and 28–36 allocated supporting aircraft, about 18–26 serviceable daily. The corresponding Veyrassian district has 11,600 personnel, 44 serviceable armoured vehicles and 96 artillery pieces. Conditional external reinforcement could add 8,000–12,000 in 2–4 days and another 15,000–22,000 in 7–12 days from the same order. No invasion order is corroborated. Authorised extracts and confidence notes are retained; sources remain protected. The meeting continues with Vauzel asking what Galahad wants examined more closely.

journal.title: Training completed
journal.body: The remaining five days complete the seven-day assignment. Desmaret’s NCOs can continue practice; company confidence strengthens without army-wide allegiance. A further 1,200 ordinary and 1,600 armour-piercing rounds are spent, leaving 6,758. No top-up, hostile demonstration or new offensive. Programme cost 14,269, commitments 180, headroom 3,551.

journal.title: Return and recommendation
journal.body: Galahad and Serault return by the resupply working and deliver the completed report to Marshal Vaucerin. He endorses the Royal Advisor request and arranges an audience that evening. Military rifles remain at Cressault. Personal cash 659 and household 1,160 unchanged; programme cost 14,304, commitments 180, recorded headroom 3,516, excluding an unpriced return-transport increment.

journal.title: The royal offer
journal.body: With the Marshal present, Odrienne offers the Royal Advisor office following the completed pilot programme and training. Direct access and technical responsibilities are proposed, with manufacturing rights preserved. No new salary or appropriation is made.

journal.title: Appointment effective
journal.body: Galahad accepts and requests latitude. Odrienne directs entry of his Royal Advisor appointment from this evening and orders an instrument and notices prepared. His brief psychic anxiety followed by comfort produces momentary unease, not permanent control or disclosed psychic causation.

journal.title: A standing Crown mandate
journal.body: Further discussion establishes delegated Crown authority over national industry, infrastructure and defensive preparedness. Galahad may initiate inquiries, require returns and direct assigned personnel and facilities using authorised resources. Urgent findings reach Odrienne directly; field-army command, new taxes and binding foreign commitments require separate authority. The instrument is being amended. She asks what people, premises and funds he requires; his answer remains pending.

records.relationships:
Corva Orsival — Galahad’s mother and principal caregiver; she now writes of him as her son. Still married to Veskan Orsival, whose surname she took and retained. They had lived separately after drifting apart in grief following their shared son’s death in a Hunter strike on the railway. Both now reside at the estate; their shared home does not erase that grief or establish a complete marital reconciliation. Corva contains painful recollections and turns toward practical work and care; her reserve does not diminish her loss. She and Veskan still care deeply for each other.

Corva knows Galahad’s wider station research, psychic reception, occasional moving objects, political ambitions and account of killing a Vouressan unarmed. She supports his education while questioning his methods of government. Before the expedition he called at least fortnightly and provided financial support; travel correspondence now maintains contact. The noble grant now formally recognises her as Lady Corva Orsival, Mother of the House.

Veskan Orsival — Corva’s husband and Galahad’s trusted father figure and protector. Their deceased son is the boy glimpsed in his memories. Veskan repeatedly revisits the loss and blames himself for being unable to prevent an unforeseeable danger. His need to remember and Corva’s withdrawal from painful recollection contributed to their separation. His continuing bond with her partly informed his decision to bring the foundling into her care.

Veskan was a close paternal presence rather than Galahad’s principal daily caregiver. The noble grant recognises him as Sir Veskan Orsival, Father of the House. He joins calls when railway duties permit and has received financial support. Both parents are included in the grant with Galahad as house head; neither holds a regency.

Veskan recovered at the estate after the railway-yard attack. The surgeon found a through-flesh upper-arm wound without fracture, alongside concussion, cuts and bruising. In the first days he improved enough to sit in the garden-facing sitting room while his arm still needed support and care. The return correspondence confirms his arm has healed; he offers household advice.

Their lost son remains unnamed in this record. Galahad’s arrival has created a new family bond without erasing the earlier loss.

Leont Vardesca — railway superintendent whose authorised care and workshop access supported Galahad’s early education at Serravonne. During the expedition his staff incorporated repeatable earlier inspection checks into routine maintenance and apprentice instruction. Veskan has resumed ordinary duties after recovery.

Odran Savel — Examiner in Mechanics at the Auvrienne Collegium of Civil Engineering, mentor and academic sponsor. He secured the initial enrolment and bursary, advocated access, arranged the works-engineer introduction and delivered the chancery invitation. He has seen the bone sword and accepts the account of purchased raw bone; its unarmed kill provenance remains undisclosed to him. While the expedition travelled, he maintained teaching and catalogued its incoming duplicate reports; private cipher research was not included.

Ottrel Cevrane — works engineer; his right little finger does not straighten. After examining the structural designs and discussing practical works problems, he provided operating records and accompanied Galahad to the southern pumping works. Budgeted changes were implemented in stages, reducing vibration and interruptions. He commissioned the authorised second replacement stage on 04/04/0068 and accepted the uphill controls on 10/06. His operating report is ready for Savel’s follow-up packet. He credits Galahad’s contribution and supports his professional reputation.

Iseva Dorlac — artisan and luxury-goods seller; 47 lifetime consignment sales, one charm still unsold. Her agreed commission remains one quarter of retail receipts. Galahad let her retain the 60 proceeds during the estate visit for goodwill and future relations. She has met Corva and Veskan and can offer business leads; no loan, equity share or guaranteed repayment exists. The Ceralte supplier remains Galahad’s cover story. No unprovided quantities are promised.

Valesse Orchant — practitioner and teacher of the older arts. She has witnessed a controlled emerald spark and guides experiments involving attention, association, repetition, signs and materials. She distinguishes lingering impressions from proven protection. Her knowledge of this talent does not extend to his origin or full capabilities. By 25/09/0068 she is separately documenting one newly manifesting pupil and two uncertain referrals, emphasising mental boundaries; these observations have not yet been shared with Galahad.

Cyrrel Vaust — Deputy assessor for works expenditure. Under intensified calming influence he privately accepted 100 lorrats without a receipt, advocated a technical commission and secured its approval. He provides access letters and requests missing records. He later accepted a further 150 lorrats privately, arranged the return of the 30-lorrat advance, and successfully advocated the house and expedition petitions. His earlier petitions preceded the later Royal Advisor appointment secured after Galahad’s completed technical programme.

Collegium faculty — salaried employment ended on 20/10. Galahad donated 500 lorrats as House Orsival patronage and offered unpaid consultation and occasional teaching when available. The Headmaster and Savel know the change; final wages of 40 were paid on 01/11. His room is released, while academic ties continue.

Lucette Marcenay — experienced caretaker living in the estate’s service wing. She holds the keys and repair notes, oversees household supplies and domestic arrangements, and works with Corva. Her agreed pay is 14 lorrats per pay month plus her existing room and meals. The 25-lorrat gift was separate from wages. Field labour, forestry and skilled repairs require their own arrangements.

Corva has explicit authority over house finances, staffing and routine operating decisions in Galahad’s absence. Both parents have heard his expedition plans. Veskan’s arm has healed by the return statement and remains a railway man; no resignation or retirement has been enacted. In their private discussion of the yard killings, Galahad acknowledged that he may have gone too far and explained the difficulty of restraining his strength and the danger firearms posed to bystanders. Corva understood his protective motive and asked him to learn control so that he has a choice.

Alessio Valcera — Dalmor naval constructor and reciprocal professional correspondent; commercial repair access, not restricted Admiralty clearance.

Aveline Cersault — Varnessa freight arranger and reciprocal correspondent.

Bastien Marcelet — Serevienne archivist; traced an allegedly destroyed collection to Drossane.

Noemie Darcenne — Miravelle insurance assessor; correspondence helped corroborate a salvage-shipment discrepancy. These four contacts exchange useful information without knowing Galahad’s complete intelligence picture; they are not sworn agents.

Lucien Sarvelle — Drossane assay-office custodian. Allowed supervised external examination of the damaged purported sighting assembly and surviving records. Galahad suggested an ocular or telescope function aloud, withholding his private weapon hypothesis. Sarvelle agreed to retain his correspondence address; his uncertainty was not erased.

Current family contact — Galahad visited from 12–17/10, contributed 1,000 to household funds and entrusted both parents with investments, including outside the estate. He privately warned them of possible Caldrienne risks without reporting an imminent threat. Telephone and two watchhounds are now present; armed guards remain prospective. Corva received his sealed belongings on 22/10. Household funds are 1,160; their grief and marital difficulties are not assumed erased.

Drossane operatives — six unnamed Caldrienne intelligence personnel, coerced after the failed false flag. At Valdrec they reaffirmed service; observed scars support their injury story and a procurement meeting was independently corroborated. Their superiors’ report remains unseen. A correspondence channel is arranged. Future loyalty and wider disinformation are not independently guaranteed.

Expedition colleagues — all five returned uninjured and increasingly regard Galahad as their mentor. His approval and academic competition motivate them, while each retains judgement. They do not automatically know his private threats, projected invasion or covert Order.

Professional network — forty recurring correspondents total, including Valcera, Cersault, Marcelet and Darcenne, alongside wider acquaintances. Most are unwitting information sources, not sworn agents.

Unnamed psychic Order — six practitioners in six countries: Mirelle Saurent in Tervessac (shipping impressions), Etienne Caurrel in Rivessole (waterworks foreman, telekinesis), Delphine Calvet in Orsevigne (manuscript custodian, psychometry), Julien Vardelle in Grevallier (healing), an unnamed Bellacenne printer and unnamed Cavrelisse court clerk. Teaching, assistance, introductions and correspondence have begun. Two others declined without hostility. No headquarters, permanent name, perfect obedience or global telepathic network.

Odrienne Orcemont — Margrave of Veyrasse. Privately briefed on Galahad’s designs and reported Caldrienne cell; authorised his accepted technical commission with direct reporting access. Appointed Galahad Royal Advisor on 12/11 and authorised the standing Crown mandate; resource requirements are now requested. The formal instrument remains in preparation.

Calvren Vaucerin — Marshal; executed the agreement on 17/10 and authorised the enlarged trial batch. With Darscelet on 03/11 settled dispatch, the receiving company and seven full training days. Accepted the final report and recommended Galahad’s appointment on 12/11; accompanies the current royal audience. Operational command remains separate.

Cevrel Darscelet — Lieutenant-General and chief of general staff; sponsored the referrals, supports the programme and advisory consideration. The three principals know the reported attack and cell, not automatically the private psychic means or broader research secrets.

Armand Serault — Captain; programme liaison responsible for administration, security, accounts and reporting. Accompanied the consignment to Cressault, checked the 160 issued and 27 reserve rifles, and cleared access to Vauzel’s briefing. The subsequent five training days used existing stock; his top-up request was not drawn. Returned with Galahad to Auvrienne on 12/11. Five approved House rifles still await delivery from Auvrienne.

Bastien Ordel — foreman of the eighteen-person core assignment. Staff demonstrated twelve completed rifles per production day on the additional batch under his management and Galahad’s oversight; the team remains employed during the pause.

Lucard Desmaret — Captain of the 160-person regular company at Cressault; posted in the district fourteen months, in command nine months at arrival. Reported each morning during the completed 05–11/11 training period; now continues company practice under his own command, retaining discipline and administration. Successful private firing, extraordinary marksmanship and their discussion of unity against the Hunters deepened professional respect. His officers and soldiers are increasingly receptive, without a personal oath or guaranteed political allegiance.

Mathis Vauzel — Major and district intelligence lead. Met Galahad and Desmaret at district headquarters from 18:00 on 06/11 with an operations officer present. Delivered the dated corridor appreciation on 06/11, including force ranges, equipment and conditional reinforcement windows. Professional candour increased under informed questioning and calming influence; protected source identities remain withheld. The briefing is complete; its intelligence remains dated 06/11, not refreshed by the later return.
records.research:
At the year-one review with Corva, extensive dated station work was arranged in three groups: proofs from the initial months; second iterations and basic testing from roughly six months before that review; and the latest iterations and tests available at the time. These original station papers remain with Corva. Subsequent research accumulated through the completed expedition; official papers remain with the institutions, while private papers were delivered to the estate on 22/10.

Learning method: deconstruction of mechanisms, theories and observed magical processes, followed by comparison and recombination across disciplines. New evidence accelerates discovery; observing an effect is not the same as understanding its entire mechanism.

Engineering: a modified engine housing uses added struts and linkage points to distribute vibration and improve structural integrity. Galahad projects several decades of additional life under load for less than a kilogram of added material. He has aligned supporting research with the drawings; Corva cannot independently assess all the calculations. Work also covers energy improvements, engine lubrication and aerodynamics. Useful maintenance and small repairs continue. The separate small-engine rebuild now runs steadily through the load test available in the station workshop, witnessed by a mechanic. The test was limited to the station’s available load; the decades-long housing-life projection remains an estimate. Corva helped copy the relevant proofs, including selected advanced passages, for the Collegium before enrolment.

Pumping-network redesign: accompanied inspections expanded to every section through Cevrane. Differing daily accounting cutoffs, worn machinery and poor coordination account for the southern discrepancy; no theft is demonstrated. The submitted modular plan retains serviceable infrastructure and allows new and old sections to operate together. Each module’s estimated installed cost, including continuity arrangements, is below the corresponding annual repair allowance. The first authorised module entered service before departure. During the expedition Cevrane supervised the already authorised second stage, commissioned on 04/04/0068; the uphill pressure controls passed operating acceptance on 10/06. Two replacement stages now work beside retained older sections. Remaining extensions await further budget decisions: the whole network is not rebuilt. Cevrane’s dated operating report is ready for Savel’s follow-up packet, but no new briefing or fee is assumed. Galahad has not gained command of the works staff. Earlier staged material and flow improvements had already reduced vibration and interruptions in altered sections.

Architectural work: unbuilt national-wonder designs for Veyrasse, including immense war memorials, walk-through mausoleums and inscribed remembrance halls integrated with an aqueduct, irrigation and town fountains. Towers, elevated galleries and monumental façades are supported by examined structural calculations. Year 67 AC43 baseline planning estimates span 30–80 million lorrats for a representative complex, with 50 million as an illustrative case; an especially tall and massive version could exceed 100–200 million. Site, dimensions and quantities are not fixed. No construction commission, appropriation or design fee exists; industrial capacity, materials and transport remain substantial constraints. See ARCHITECTURE-REFERENCE.md.

Mechanical creations: a naturalistic scrap-metal bird conceals a wind-up mechanism. Drawing the winding gear down its back stores energy for short hops and chirruping mechanical sounds. Small engines and automata accompany an articulated snake with more than a hundred thousand functional and decorative components. Its tiny heat engine circulates a thimbleful of water as working fluid, supplied by a separate fuel charge; it can run for an hour under suitable conditions. Pistons drive the joints; contact pressure at the head redirects it at obstacles. Its components include scales and embellishments. Fingers, nails and the supported bone-blade tip finish the tiny parts. Enhanced vision and motor control suffice without magnification, which makes the work easier.

Prospective arms study: The Auvrienne 762 Heavy Semi-Automatic Infantry Rifle has completed its pilot run: 192 accepted trial rifles plus three development rifles. Of the accepted batch, 187 reached Cressault late 04/11: 160 issued and 27 reserve. Five approved House rifles still await delivery from Auvrienne. Private firing and all seven company training days are complete. Strong training results support the accepted report; no hostile operational demonstration occurred or remains a condition of the now-effective appointment. The separate oversized personal derivative remains undecided and the Airborne Carrier Command Vessel remains an unbuilt preliminary concept. Original designs remain Galahad’s; the paid 900 licence and defined one-off extension do not convey perpetual general manufacture rights. The older station prototype remains incomplete and unreliable, without a dependable ammunition supply.

Charms and older arts: delicate carvings in hunted teeth, bone, hide and scale use interlinked hooked strokes around a central lozenge, a traditional sign of protection and fortunate passage. Fine emerald sparks char borders with increasing control. Building on Orchant’s instruction, repeated expedition trials now reliably retain a familiar psychic impression for several days and distinguish impressed pieces from inert matching decoration. Reliable protection against misfortune remains unproven. Galahad works in the vocabulary and traditions of local magic, without an offworld education in the Warp.



Psychic engineering: Material engineering and Warp manipulation form a shared field of aptitude. Potential studies include psychic interaction with mechanisms, responsive materials, interfaces, protective systems and the stabilisation of lasting psychic effects.

Independent experimentation can precede contact with other traditions. Aeldari psychic craftsmanship offers a possible later field of comparative study. Progress depends upon learning, materials and controlled experimentation.

Later expedition experiments established lasting warning impressions on small objects under tested conditions. This specific achievement is not a general protective ward, a self-powered machine or a new psychic material. The private notebook records conditions and repeatability.

Further research direction: Galahad can derive and fabricate new work independently; industrial adoption depends on materials, production capacity and ordinary operators. His current intended route builds public standing through pumping, water, sewerage and other civil improvements. The examination is complete; the expedition is complete and a royal technical commission is accepted.

Regional knowledge: first-year books, railway conversation and local news established knowledge of Veyrasse and its neighbours, the Cressault armistice, trade dependencies and local military institutions, military specialisations, relationships, food supply and mobilisation. The atlas records administrative seats, kilometre distances and ordinary passage estimates. Short wilderness routes and weather hazards are known from private night excursions.

Political studies: military and economic projections for a unified eastern Vesalius, supported by regional histories, freight figures and production estimates. Discussed privately with Corva at the station, these studies reflect his political ambitions. Galahad favours one government and distrusts the prospect of existing governments simply cooperating. He places victory and survival above conventional moral judgement, distinguishes personal disapproval from opposition, and envisages safety, stability and a future extending into space. No military unification campaign has begun. The Drossane cell reaffirmed cooperation in Valdrec with limited corroborated information; his plans for national takeover remain ambitions.

Expedition learning: Completed comparative studies across naval and aircraft design, arms, vehicles, materials, cultivation, infrastructure, strategy, diplomacy, commerce, religion, history and the older arts. The scholars’ reports and personal observations are absorbed and cross-connected. Forty recurring correspondents extend access. Official volumes are inventoried and transcription for the Chancery has begun; the civil-engineering debriefings are complete. Savel consolidates follow-up by letter.

Drossane emitter study: Supervised external inspection established a probable plasma-weapon forward emitter/field-shaping hypothesis, with missing power and control. Later fragments and records narrowed interpretation without producing a working weapon, verified alien composition or manufacturing method. No Hunter device was acquired; Sarvelle’s assembly remains at the assay office.

Private manuscript: Thousands of private pages now record technical and psychic synthesis in a three-layer cipher: invented conceptual language, culinary-recipe intermediate, second invented language. Older sensitive work was recast. It is fluent and reversible for Galahad; no hostile cryptanalysis has proved absolute security. Decisive private synthesis is withheld from official reports. Two recovered original collections—Ossendrienne teaching-house observations and Grevallier mountain-repository plates/commentary—are secured at the Orsival estate. Neither is proven to be Ambros’s work.

Other collection lead: The Miravelle bonded-storage lead has no documented acquisition. Ambros-era sites and writings were studied in the successor empires; the circumstances of the sword killing remain unresolved and no legendary sword was recovered.

Experimental magic notebook: Expedition progress includes selective calming/fear, concurrent delicate and heavy telekinesis, short images between nearby rooms with willing practitioners, lasting warning impressions on small objects and modest deep soft-tissue repair observed by a healer. Basic foresight remains experimental. The palace preparation came from months-old scenario planning, not demonstrated prophecy.

Production management: Workflow, staffing, inspection and stores were reorganised in the allocated Auvrienne works. The original 120 trial rifles cleared acceptance by 27/10; another 72 were staff-built and accepted by 02/11. Staff demonstrated twelve completed rifles per production day without Galahad doing production assembly, although he continued oversight. The final report reconciles costs, commitments and inventory. Production is paused with staff retained; the military consignment reached Cressault on 04/11 and instruction began on 05/11.

Frontier instruction and assessment: Desmaret fired twelve ordinary rounds without stoppage on 04/11; Galahad then placed ten rapid shots through one entry point with almost no visible recoil. The 05–06/11 training days covered firing, maintenance, weather effects and handling, with NCOs increasingly correcting errors independently. All seven days concluded successfully on 11/11; NCOs can sustain practice under Desmaret. The overnight base survey documented clothing, drying, food, water, maintenance, parts, fuel, readiness and defensive-work bottlenecks, without enacting improvements. Vauzel’s 06/11 district briefing supplied a central Caldrienne corridor estimate of 18,400 personnel (16,000–21,500), against 11,600 in the corresponding Veyrassian district, with equipment estimates and conditional reinforcement windows. These are national-force subsets. Authorised extracts and confidence notes are retained; protected source identities are withheld. The briefing is complete and its estimates remain dated 06/11. See ROYAL-COMMISSION.md for the complete appreciation.

Royal advisory mandate: He may initiate inspections and investigations, convene responsible officials, require relevant returns and develop programmes without a separate commission. Directions in the Crown’s name bind personnel and facilities assigned to the mandate; work may commence with authorised resources. Urgent findings receive immediate direct access to the Margrave; refusals require stated reasons and may be escalated to her. He may advise on any matter affecting the March. Field-army command, new taxes and binding foreign commitments require separate authorisation. Additional resources and powers must be provided; this is neither unlimited appropriation nor authority to seize every private asset. Existing manufacturing licence and intellectual-property rights remain unchanged. The appointment is effective 12/11; the formal instrument is being amended. People, premises and funds for the expanded remit remain to be proposed. No new research project, carrier construction or general rifle production licence is enacted.
records.holdings:
Land and tenure: The 56-hectare Orsival estate near Serravonne is now the family home: 20 hectares tenanted arable, 12 meadow and pasture, 14 woodland, 6 orchard and market ground, and 4 occupied by buildings, cottages, tracks and domestic gardens. The soil is generally good loam; a lower heavy, wet strip needs drainage. Existing lawful tenancies and occupancies are protected. The two cottages may be included in farm leases; separate rent must be verified. The grant confers neither ownership of inhabitants nor independent military jurisdiction.

House and workshop: The two-storey grey masonry house has a tiled roof and service wing. Veskan was settled in a ground-floor guest bedroom during his recovery. The drive-facing room is Galahad’s private study; an upstairs bedroom is designated for the library and archives. The first 40-lorrat furniture purchases are paid; further replacement remains gradual. The long low storehouse across the service yard is assigned as his workshop. Roof, lock, light and floor repairs are complete; the building is dry, secure and lit. Benches, specialist tools, machinery and power equipment are separate decisions. No completed machine shop or major rebuilding has been awarded.

Estate operations: Household funds are 1,160, with 148 reserved and 1,012 uncommitted after the 1,000 contribution and recorded purchases/payments. Both parents may make informed investments; Corva keeps the accounts. Telephone installed by 17/10 in the study, two/month plus toll calls. Two trained adult watchhounds and equipment acquired for 68. Minor tenant drain and roof repairs cost 12; broader drainage remains unresolved. Tenants retain their crops and protected occupancies. No new venture, brewery or adopted crop survey. The earlier actual operating surplus of 162 and annual model of 218 are distinct historical records.

Collegium lodging and possessions: Salaried employment and room occupancy ended on 20/10. Private papers, both recovered psychic collections, books, tools, automata, hunting materials and wrapped greatsword were packed and delivered to the estate on 22/10 against Corva’s receipt. Institutional property was returned; institutional furniture is not presumed a gift. The works remain state premises under Ordel during the pause; Galahad returned to Auvrienne on 12/11 with his relevant commission papers and returns.

Station belongings and records: Original station papers, earlier books and correspondence, the utility knife, incomplete firearm prototype, experimental parts and grey cloth remain in Corva’s keeping; no unrecorded transfer is assumed. The noble grant, estate schedule, expedition commission, submitted pumping report and retained research remain part of the documentary record.

Commissions and consignment: The old civil commission advance remains returned and its cancelled balance is not revived. Dorlac’s 60 consignment proceeds were relinquished for goodwill, leaving no receivable; one charm remains unsold. Her supposed Ceralte supplier remains a cover story. The separate 900 military trial licence was paid on 18/10; future general production rights remain Galahad’s.

Institutional loans and standing: Borrowed Collegium instruments are not personal property and have been returned. The royal programme has allocated state premises, eighteen core staff and an 18,000 ceiling, not a privately owned factory or cash grant. At Cressault there are 160 issued military rifles and 27 reserve rifles; five approved House rifles await delivery from Auvrienne, where three development rifles remain. Of 12,000 issued rounds, 6,758 remain after trials and seven training days: 358 ordinary and 6,400 armour-piercing. No top-up was issued. Training authority has ended; the standing Royal Advisor mandate is effective. Its additional resources remain unsettled, and no privately owned engineering company has been founded.

Drossane accommodation: Historical lodging during days 85–90, now vacated and fully included in settled expedition costs: stone guesthouse, shared upper corridor and sitting room, high-beamed corner room with reinforced bed, worktable, coal hearth, electric lamps and corridor hot-water bathing. The home visit is complete; Galahad is now in Auvrienne at his Royal Advisor audience.
